children: 0954 GMT - The 2.5% rise in German manufacturing orders in July looks goods news but only at first glance, Commerzbank economist Marco Wagner says in a note. Excluding large orders worth more than 50 million euros, orders fell on month by 1.4%. "This means the underlying trend continues to move sideways at a low level," Wagner says. Looking at the core trend that excludes the larger orders, the recovery that had begun to take hold has once again fizzled out, he says. That means a recovery in German industrial production is unlikely for the time being, especially given low water levels in the Rhine River in recent weeks and the fact that energy prices have risen again. "The German economy will therefore recover only moderately," he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

0948 GMT - The Gulf's push to build new trade, energy and logistics infrastructure is likely to continue regardless of the near-term outcome of the Iran war, the Arab Gulf States Institute says. Bypassing the Strait of Hormuz is one objective, but the investment drive extends to pipelines, railways, roads, ports and new economic corridors across the region, says ASGI non-resident fellow Robert Mogielnicki. Saudi Arabia stands to benefit from a westward shift in economic activity, while the U.A.E. is developing eastern export and logistics hubs and Oman is gaining from routes that avoid regional chokepoints. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

0929 GMT - Gulf corporate sentiment rebounded in the second quarter despite continued disruption from the Iran war, investor-relations advisory firm Iridium Advisors says. Its GCC Earnings Call Sentiment Index rose 17% to 34.5 points across 150 calls held in July and August, the first increase since the conflict began. Management-presentation sentiment rose 15% to 45.7 points, above its long-term average, while analyst Q&A sentiment remained below its historical norm. Qatar posted the strongest country improvement at 45%, followed by Saudi Arabia at 27% and the U.A.E. at 9%. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

0916 GMT - Sterling could weaken in the lead-up to the budget on October 28 due to renewed political concerns, Ebury's Matthew Ryan says in a note. The government's ambitious spending plans could mean an increase in tax rates and higher debt issuance, measures which could raise U.K. political risk, Ryan says. "The political risk now seems to be grossly underappreciated ahead of the autumn budget," he says. Sterling last trades steady at $1.3525. The euro is also flat at 0.8589 pounds. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0844 GMT - Philippine inflation this year is likely to undershoot the central bank's projections, Barclays economist Brian Tan says in a note. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas forecast full-year inflation at 6.1% during its August meeting, implying that price increases would average between 7.5% and 7.6% for August to December. Headline CPI rose 6.1% in August. After the August print came in above expectations, Barclays raises its 2026 inflation forecast to 5.6% from 5.4%, also taking into account elevated global oil prices. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0818 GMT - Investors await the Bank of England Decision Maker Panel data set to be released at 0830 GMT for clues on the possible inflationary impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict on U.K. businesses, RBC Capital Markets strategists say in a note. The Decision Maker Panel is a survey of chief financial officers from small, medium and large U.K. businesses on their views on inflation and wage growth. "The BOE's internal surveys are taking on greater importance in terms of its decision making," the strategists say. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0751 GMT - Yields on U.K. government bonds rise slightly, reversing some of the previous day's falls as focus turns to key U.S. jobs data at 1230 GMT amid uncertainty over the timing of a possible U.S. interest-rate rise. Meanwhile, oil prices remain elevated, keeping alive concerns about inflation. Middle East tensions and the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz are contributing to rising energy prices. Investors fully price in two quarter-point interest-rate rises by the Bank of England by March 2027, LSEG data show. The price of a barrel of Brent crude edges down 0.4% but remains high at $95.11. Ten-year gilt yields rise 0.6 basis points to last trade at 5.157%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0714 GMT - Bitcoin's short-term price moves would likely depend on the Fed's interest rate path, after the cryptocurrency topped $80,000 on Thursday, says Mariia Menahem, chief executive of Clarity Global, in a note. Markets are pricing in lower rate hike expectations, as hiring by U.S. private-sector employers saw softer growth in August, she says. Lower rates reduce the appeal of cash and fixed-income assets, weaken the dollar and improve liquidity conditions for risk assets such as bitcoin. Bitcoin is 0.75% lower at $80,874.56, according to LSEG data.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0714 GMT - Bitcoin declines modestly, after climbing above $82,000 overnight, the highest level since May. Bitcoin accelerated overnight after U.S. Federal Reserve member Chris Waller said he would vote for rates to stay on hold if inflation continues to improve, causing the dollar to weaken. Bitcoin falls 0.8% to last trade at $80,848, after rising to $82,164 overnight, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0656 GMT - Eurozone government bond yields rise slightly after dropping the previous session as investors await fresh impulse from U.S. employment data at 1230 GMT. Friday's eurozone economic data calendar is empty, and there is no government bond issuance either, other than Belgium's optional reverse inquiry auction. The focus, however, will gradually turn to the European Central Bank's meeting on Sept. 10, where a 25-basis-point rate hike is fully priced, according to LSEG. The 10-year German Bund yield rises 1.0 basis points to 3.361%, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0655 GMT - China's industrial production likely grew in August, according to BofA Securities in a research note. Industrial production likely edged up to 4.7% year-over-year in August from 4.5% in July, the bank says. This is reflected in the official manufacturing PMI production index, which returned to expansion as extreme-weather disruptions eased, the bank says. "Continued strength in high-tech and equipment manufacturing likely supported activity, although weak mining and basic-materials production capped the recovery," BofA says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0653 GMT - The dollar rises slightly after dropping significantly on Thursday following comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support holding interest rates steady if inflation data back this up. Market attention turns to key U.S. nonfarm payrolls data at 1230 GMT. A strong jobs reading could revive expectations for a Fed rate hike, boosting the dollar, while weak data could increase prospects of unchanged rates and send the currency lower. Investors are cautious due to uncertainty around payroll growth, inflation and the next interest-rate decision, says Clarity Global CEO Mariia Menahem in a note. The DXY dollar index rises 0.1% to 98.989, having dropped to a 10-day low of 98.831 on Thursday. (jessica.fleetham@wsj.com)
